title: Reduction techniques for the derived delooping levels
summary: The derived delooping level is a recently introduced homological invariant that provides an upper bound for the finitistic dimension of the opposite algebra. In this paper, we employ two reduction techniques-cleft extensions and recollements-to study the finiteness of the derived delooping level of finite-dimensional algebras over a field. By applying the theory of cleft extensions to bound quiver algebras, we establish arrow-removal operations that preserve the finiteness of the derived delooping level.
